name: Karet (Excision from the World-to-Come)
notes: The 36 categories of transgression punishable by karet, their enumeration, and the distinction between intentional (karet) and unwitting (sin offering) violation

name: Asham Talui (Provisional Guilt Offering)
notes: The provisional guilt offering brought when one is uncertain whether they committed a sin requiring a sin offering; rules of when it applies, when it atones, and what happens if certainty is later established

name: Sliding-Scale Offering — Detailed Rules (Oleh v'Yored)
notes: Detailed rules of the sliding-scale offering: the five categories obligated (false oath of testimony, false oath on deposit, defiling the Temple or its foods, woman after childbirth, leper); substitution between animal, bird, and flour depending on financial status

name: Offering of a Woman after Childbirth (Korban Yoledet)
notes: Detailed rules of which types of miscarriage or birth obligate a sin offering, including sandal fetus, placenta, amniotic sac, caesarean birth; cases of uncertainty; aggregation of multiple births into one offering

name: Mechusar Kapparah — Detailed Rules
notes: The four categories of mechusar kapparah (zav, zava, woman after childbirth, leper) and their inability to eat sacrificial meat until the atonement offering is brought; also nazirite and convert in this context

name: Lapse of Awareness (He'elem) in Sin Offering Liability
notes: Rules governing what constitutes a single lapse of awareness for purposes of sin offering liability; whether multiple transgressions in one lapse require one or multiple offerings; combining different prohibitions

name: Doubt in Sin Offering Liability (Safek Chatat)
notes: Cases of doubt whether one committed a sin requiring a sin offering, including mixed pieces of forbidden/permitted food, uncertainty about Shabbat vs. weekday labor; dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua

name: Doubt in Misuse of Consecrated Property (Safek Meilah)
notes: Rabbi Akiva's position that a provisional guilt offering is brought for uncertainty about meilah; dispute with Rabbis; Rabbi Tarfon's alternative procedure of paying immediately with conditional guilt offering

name: Discovery of Innocence After Bringing Offering
notes: What happens to a provisional or definite guilt offering when it is discovered that no sin was committed: before/after slaughter, before/after blood sprinkling; dispute between Rabbi Meir, Rabbis, Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yosei

name: Guilt Offering of the Pious (Asham Chasidim)
notes: Rabbi Eliezer's view that one may voluntarily bring a provisional guilt offering at any time; the practice of Bava ben Buta who brought one daily; dispute with the Rabbis who limit the provisional guilt offering to actual cases of doubt

name: Yom Kippur Atoning for Uncertain Sins
notes: Yom Kippur exempts one from bringing a provisional guilt offering for uncertainties that arose even at nightfall ending the day; sin offerings and definite guilt offerings are not exempted by Yom Kippur

name: Measure and Time for Forbidden Eating (Shiur Achilah)
notes: The time span within which consumption of an olive-bulk creates liability; dispute between Rabbi Meir (time to eat toasted grain) and Rabbis (time to eat a half-loaf); also the quarter-log of wine for a priest entering the Temple

name: Multiple Liabilities from a Single Act of Intercourse
notes: Talmudic analysis of how a single act of forbidden intercourse can incur multiple separate sin offering liabilities when the woman stands in multiple prohibited relationship categories to the man simultaneously

name: Espoused Maidservant (Shifcha Charufah)
notes: Halakhot of the half-slave half-free betrothed maidservant; the guilt offering brought for intercourse with her; distinctions from other forbidden relationships regarding punishment, offering type, and conditions for liability

name: Blood Prohibition — Detailed Categories
notes: Detailed enumeration of which blood is forbidden (slaughter blood, blood of stabbing, blood that departs with the soul) vs. which is permitted (spleen, heart, eggs, grasshoppers, tamtzit exudate blood); dispute of Rabbi Yehuda on exudate blood

name: Designation of Offering for Specific Sin (Kavvanat HaKorban)
notes: A sin offering may not be redirected to atone for a different sin than originally designated; one's heirs may not bring a designated sin offering in place of the decedent; derived from 'for his sin that he sinned'

name: Equality of Father and Mother in Honor Obligation
notes: Rabbi Shimon's exposition that Torah alternates order of father/mother and mother/father to show equality, yet concludes the father's honor takes precedence because both son and mother are obligated to honor the father; teacher's honor vis-à-vis father

name: Nazirite's Offering for Impurity (Korban Nazir Tamei)
notes: The nazirite who became ritually impure brings an offering for intentional impurity the same as for unwitting impurity; the nazirite's mechusar kapparah status until offerings are sacrificed

name: Two Partners Bringing One Atonement Offering
notes: Dispute whether two people who each may have committed a sin can jointly bring one sin offering or guilt offering as partners with a stipulation; Rabbi Shimon permits it conditionally; Rabbi Yosei prohibits conditional atonement offerings
